title: Chemical Equations and Stoichiometry

cards.b: A cook knows that two eggs and a cup of flour give a certain number of pancakes. Chemists do the same with atoms. Stoichiometry is the arithmetic of reactions: how much of each ingredient you need, and how much product you get. It runs fertiliser plants, medicine factories and your car's engine.

Antoine Lavoisier, 1789, showed that in a closed system mass is conserved. Atoms rearrange; none are created or destroyed. So every chemical equation must be balanced: same number of each atom on both sides.

Also, Joseph Proust (1799) found that a compound always has the same mass ratio of elements. Water is always 1 part hydrogen to 8 parts oxygen by mass.

Hydrogen burns in oxygen. Unbalanced: H2 + O2 → H2O (2 O on the left, 1 on the right).

  1. Put 2 in front of H2O: H2 + O2 → 2H2O. Now O is balanced.
  2. H is now 4 on right, so put 2 before H2.

2H2 + O2 → 2H2O. Never change small subscripts (that changes the substance); only change the big coefficients in front.

The numbers in 2H2 + O2 → 2H2O mean 2 mol H2 react with 1 mol O2 to give 2 mol H2O. In grams: 4 g H2 + 32 g O2 → 36 g water. Mass in = mass out (4 + 32 = 36).

Another: N2 + 3H2 → 2NH3 (ammonia). 1 mol nitrogen needs 3 mol hydrogen, giving 2 mol ammonia.
Almost every problem follows the same path.

If you have 10 bread slices and 3 cheese slices, you can make only 3 sandwiches. Cheese is the limiting reagent: it runs out first and caps the product. The other is in excess.

Percent yield = (actual yield / theoretical yield) x 100. Real reactions seldom give 100 percent, because of side reactions and losses.

cards.h: How much water from 4 g hydrogen?
cards.b:
1. Moles of H2 = 4 / 2 = 2 mol.
  2. 2H2 → 2H2O is a 1:1 ratio, so 2 mol H2O.
  3. Mass = 2 x 18 = 36 g.

Limiting reagent test: 4 g H2 with 16 g O2. Moles H2 = 2; moles O2 = 0.5. H2 needs half as much O2: 2 mol H2 needs 1 mol O2. We have only 0.5, so O2 is limiting. Water made = 2 x 0.5 = 1 mol = 18 g.

• Do not balance by changing subscripts. H2O2 is not H2O.
  • Coefficients are mole ratios, not mass ratios.
  • The limiting reagent is not the one with less mass but the one that runs out first in mole terms.
  • Mass is conserved, moles are not always. 3 mol reactants can become 2 mol product.

Ammonia from N2 + 3H2 → 2NH3 (the Haber-Bosch process) is the base of urea fertiliser. India's first large fertiliser plant at Sindri (now in Jharkhand) began producing in 1951, backing the push for food security. Plants calculate stoichiometry daily: how much natural gas, air and steam give each tonne of urea. India is among the world's largest fertiliser consumers.

• Balance equations by coefficients so atoms match.
  • Coefficients give mole ratios; convert grams to moles and back.
  • Limiting reagent controls the product; percent yield compares real to theoretical.
